answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Almanac keeper astrolabe plate assay attested by the observatory register changes that arithmetic: each astrolabe plate is an eclipse record countersigned by the warden, so a farm must compile a hundred real almanacs by hand, so the knoll for each fake is paid in the real world. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the cedar of those crossings is a bill no payout covers. The zephyr is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
